From 8ecd06277a7664f4ef018abae3abd3451d64e7a6 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Jozsef Kadlecsik <kadlec@netfilter.org>
Date: Mon, 17 Jun 2024 11:18:15 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] netfilter: ipset: Fix suspicious rcu_dereference_protected()

When destroying all sets, we are either in pernet exit phase or
are executing a "destroy all sets command" from userspace. The latter
was taken into account in ip_set_dereference() (nfnetlink mutex is held),
but the former was not. The patch adds the required check to
rcu_dereference_protected() in ip_set_dereference().

Fixes: 4e7aaa6b82d6 ("netfilter: ipset: Fix race between namespace cleanup and gc in the list:set type")
Reported-by: syzbot+b62c37cdd58103293a5a@syzkaller.appspotmail.com
Reported-by: syzbot+cfbe1da5fdfc39efc293@syzkaller.appspotmail.com
Reported-by: kernel test robot <oliver.sang@intel.com>
Closes: https://lore.kernel.org/oe-lkp/202406141556.e0b6f17e-lkp@intel.com
Signed-off-by: Jozsef Kadlecsik <kadlec@netfilter.org>
Signed-off-by: Pablo Neira Ayuso <pablo@netfilter.org>

diff --git a/net/netfilter/ipset/ip_set_core.c b/net/netfilter/ipset/ip_set_core.c
index c7ae4d9bf3d2..61431690cbd5 100644
--- a/net/netfilter/ipset/ip_set_core.c
+++ b/net/netfilter/ipset/ip_set_core.c
@@ -53,12 +53,13 @@ MODULE_DESCRIPTION("core IP set support");
 MODULE_ALIAS_NFNL_SUBSYS(NFNL_SUBSYS_IPSET);
 
 /* When the nfnl mutex or ip_set_ref_lock is held: */
-#define ip_set_dereference(p)		\
-	rcu_dereference_protected(p,	\
+#define ip_set_dereference(inst)	\
+	rcu_dereference_protected((inst)->ip_set_list,	\
 		lockdep_nfnl_is_held(NFNL_SUBSYS_IPSET) || \
-		lockdep_is_held(&ip_set_ref_lock))
+		lockdep_is_held(&ip_set_ref_lock) || \
+		(inst)->is_deleted)
 #define ip_set(inst, id)		\
-	ip_set_dereference((inst)->ip_set_list)[id]
+	ip_set_dereference(inst)[id]
 #define ip_set_ref_netlink(inst,id)	\
 	rcu_dereference_raw((inst)->ip_set_list)[id]
 #define ip_set_dereference_nfnl(p)	\
@@ -1133,7 +1134,7 @@ static int ip_set_create(struct sk_buff *skb, const struct nfnl_info *info,
 		if (!list)
 			goto cleanup;
 		/* nfnl mutex is held, both lists are valid */
-		tmp = ip_set_dereference(inst->ip_set_list);
+		tmp = ip_set_dereference(inst);
 		memcpy(list, tmp, sizeof(struct ip_set *) * inst->ip_set_max);
 		rcu_assign_pointer(inst->ip_set_list, list);
 		/* Make sure all current packets have passed through */
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `net/netfilter/ipset/ip_set_core.c`**
1. The macro `ip_set_dereference` has been modified to include an additional condition that checks if the instance (`inst`) is deleted. The new definition is:
   ```c
   #define ip_set_dereference(inst) \
       rcu_dereference_protected((inst)->ip_set_list, \
           lockdep_nfnl_is_held(NFNL_SUBSYS_IPSET) || \
           lockdep_is_held(&ip_set_ref_lock) || \
           (inst)->is_deleted)
   ```
   This change ensures that the reference to `ip_set_list` is safely dereferenced even when the instance is marked as deleted.

2. The usage of `ip_set_dereference` in the `ip_set_create` function has been updated to pass the entire instance (`inst`) instead of just `inst->ip_set_list`. The line:
   ```c
   tmp = ip_set_dereference(inst->ip_set_list);
   ```
   has been changed to:
   ```c
   tmp = ip_set_dereference(inst);
   ```

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modifications in the `ip_set_core.c` file are closely related as they both address the handling of the `ip_set_list` during the destruction of sets. The primary change is the enhancement of the `ip_set_dereference` macro to include a check for whether the instance is deleted, which is crucial for preventing potential race conditions when dereferencing pointers in a concurrent environment. The update in the `ip_set_create` function reflects this change by ensuring that the correct instance is passed to the macro, thereby maintaining the integrity of the dereferencing operation during the creation of IP sets. Overall, these modifications work together to improve the safety and reliability of the code when managing IP sets in the netfilter framework.

```c

	rcu_dereference_protected(p,	
```

Reason:
The bug occurs due to a race condition when destroying all sets, particularly during the pernet exit phase or when executing a "destroy all sets" command from userspace. The original implementation of `ip_set_dereference()` did not account for the scenario where the instance might be deleted, leading to unsafe dereferencing of the `ip_set_list` pointer without proper protection, which could result in accessing invalid memory.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
#define ip_set_dereference(inst)	\
	rcu_dereference_protected((inst)->ip_set_list,	
```
```c
+		lockdep_is_held(&ip_set_ref_lock) || \
+		(inst)->is_deleted)
```
Reason:
The patch modifies the `ip_set_dereference()` macro to include an additional check for the `is_deleted` flag of the instance. This ensures that the dereference operation is protected against accessing the `ip_set_list` when the instance is in the process of being deleted, thus preventing potential invalid memory access and fixing the race condition.
